references.text: The command to help the poor and the foreigner, reflecting God's care for those in need in Israel.
The obligation to support a brother who has become poor by opening your hand to him.
The immediate context that warns against closing your hand to the poor brother and commands generosity.
The blessing upon those who care for the poor and weak.
A warning against despising your neighbor who is poor, and the blessing of showing mercy.
Whoever gives to the poor lends to the Lord, and He will repay them.
Jesus quotes this verse when he says that the poor will always be with you.
Jesus refers to this verse in connection with the anointing at Bethany.
Jesus' quotation of this verse in response to Judas' criticism of Mary.
Paul's commitment to remember the poor, in line with the Old Testament command.
An exhortation not to close your heart to a brother in need, but to show practical love.
